title: Historical significance
subject: Historical thinking
keywords: Judge significance using impact, duration, relevance, and what it reveals about the past.
summary: The importance assigned to an event, person, development, or idea.

title: Primary source
subject: Evidence
keywords: Evaluate creator, purpose, audience, context, limitations, and corroboration.
summary: Evidence created during the period studied or by a direct participant or witness.

title: Cause and consequence
subject: Historical thinking
keywords: Distinguish long-term conditions, immediate triggers, intended effects, and unintended consequences.
summary: The relationship between conditions or actions and the results that followed.

title: Continuity and change
subject: Historical thinking
keywords: Consider pace, direction, turning points, and differences among groups.
summary: What remained similar and what changed across time.

title: Treaties and treaty relationships
subject: Canada
keywords: Study written and oral understandings, historical context, implementation, and continuing legal and moral responsibilities.
summary: Agreements between Indigenous nations and the Crown establishing ongoing rights, responsibilities, and relationships.

title: Canadian Confederation
subject: Canada
keywords: Examine political compromise, economics, defence, federalism, expansion, and effects on peoples excluded from negotiations.
summary: The 1867 union that created the Dominion of Canada from four provinces.

title: Industrial Revolution
subject: World history
keywords: It transformed labour, class, population, empire, technology, and the environment.
summary: A long shift toward mechanized production, factories, urbanization, and new transportation systems.

title: Imperialism
subject: World history
keywords: It may involve settlement, force, unequal trade, resource extraction, and cultural suppression.
summary: The extension of political, economic, or cultural control over other peoples or territories.

title: First World War
subject: Canada & World
keywords: Analyze militarism, alliances, imperialism, nationalism, total war, home fronts, and consequences.
summary: A global war fought mainly from 1914 to 1918 among rival alliances.

title: Great Depression
subject: Canada & World
keywords: Study financial instability, falling demand, unemployment, drought, poverty, and policy responses.
summary: A severe worldwide economic downturn beginning in 1929 and lasting through much of the 1930s.

title: Second World War
subject: Canada & World
keywords: Core issues include fascism, aggression, the Holocaust, genocide, resistance, total war, and postwar institutions.
summary: A global war from 1939 to 1945 between the Axis and Allied powers.

title: Cold War
subject: World history
keywords: It included nuclear deterrence, proxy wars, alliances, propaganda, espionage, and science competition.
summary: A long geopolitical and ideological rivalry after 1945, especially between the United States and Soviet Union.

title: Truth and Reconciliation
subject: Canada
keywords: Centre survivor testimony, Indigenous rights, the Calls to Action, local treaty relationships, and present responsibilities.
summary: An ongoing process of truth-telling, acknowledgement, repair, and renewed relationships after colonial harms, including residential schools.

title: Latitude and longitude
subject: Map skills
keywords: Latitude measures north or south of the equator; longitude measures east or west of the prime meridian.
summary: A coordinate system used to describe locations on Earth.

title: Geographic Information System (GIS)
subject: Geospatial skills
keywords: GIS layers can combine population, land use, transport, hazards, and environmental information.
summary: A system for storing, analyzing, and displaying geographically referenced data.

title: Population density
subject: Human geography
keywords: Density does not show how evenly people are distributed inside an area.
summary: Population divided by land area.

title: Urbanization
subject: Human geography
keywords: Analyze employment, migration, infrastructure, housing, environment, and inequality.
summary: Growth in the share of people living in urban areas and expansion of cities.

title: Sustainability
subject: Environment
keywords: Good analysis examines trade-offs, equity, scale, evidence, and long-term effects.
summary: Meeting present needs while maintaining ecological, social, and economic systems for the future.

title: Democracy
subject: Government
keywords: It also depends on rights, rule of law, participation, accountability, and access to reliable information.
summary: A system in which people exercise political power directly or through elected representatives.

title: Federalism
subject: Government
keywords: Canada assigns responsibilities to federal and provincial governments; municipalities receive authority from provinces.
summary: A system dividing law-making powers between national and regional governments.

title: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
subject: Rights
keywords: Rights may involve justified limits, court interpretation, and remedies.
summary: Part of the Constitution Act, 1982 protecting specified rights and freedoms.

title: Rule of law
subject: Law
keywords: It supports accountability, due process, predictability, and limits on arbitrary power.
summary: The principle that individuals and governments are governed by publicly known laws applied through lawful institutions.

title: Public policy
subject: Citizenship
keywords: Compare goals, evidence, cost, feasibility, rights, benefits, harms, and effects on groups.
summary: A course of action chosen by government to address a public issue.

title: Thesis statement
subject: Writing
keywords: It should be specific enough to organize evidence and broad enough to support several reasons.
summary: A clear, arguable central claim answering the task and guiding the response.

title: Evidence-based paragraph
subject: Writing
keywords: PEEL, PEE, CER, and similar structures all require reasoning, not just quotation.
summary: A paragraph that makes a point, supports it, explains the evidence, and links to the argument.

title: Inference
subject: Reading
keywords: An inference must be plausible and traceable to evidence.
summary: A conclusion supported by textual clues and relevant background knowledge.

title: Tone
subject: Reading
keywords: Infer tone through diction, imagery, structure, emphasis, and context.
summary: The writer’s or speaker’s attitude toward the subject or audience.

title: Bias and framing
subject: Media literacy
keywords: Identify bias, then corroborate factual claims with other reliable evidence.
summary: The influence of perspective, selection, emphasis, language, or interests on presentation.

title: Paraphrasing
subject: Research
keywords: Read, close the source, explain from understanding, verify accuracy, and cite.
summary: Restating an idea fully in your own wording and structure while citing the source.

title: Counterargument
subject: Argument
keywords: Accurate counterarguments strengthen credibility and analysis.
summary: A relevant objection or alternative position considered fairly and answered with reasoning.

title: Scarcity
subject: Foundations
keywords: Scarcity forces choices and creates opportunity costs.
summary: Resources are limited while wants and possible uses are numerous.

title: Opportunity cost
subject: Foundations
keywords: It can include time, resources, experience, and money.
summary: The value of the best alternative given up when a choice is made.

title: Demand
subject: Markets
keywords: Price changes move along a demand curve; non-price factors shift it.
summary: Quantities consumers are willing and able to buy at various prices during a period.

title: Supply
subject: Markets
keywords: Input costs, technology, expectations, sellers, and policy can shift supply.
summary: Quantities producers are willing and able to sell at various prices during a period.

title: Market equilibrium
subject: Markets
keywords: Shortages put upward pressure on price; surpluses put downward pressure.
summary: The price and quantity where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

title: Price elasticity of demand
subject: Markets
keywords: Elastic demand changes proportionally more; inelastic demand changes less.
summary: Responsiveness of quantity demanded to a percentage change in price.

title: Gross domestic product (GDP)
subject: Macroeconomics
keywords: GDP does not measure all well-being, unpaid work, equality, or environmental quality.
summary: Market value of final goods and services produced within a country during a period.

title: Inflation
subject: Macroeconomics
keywords: It reduces purchasing power and is commonly estimated from a price index.
summary: A sustained increase in the general price level.

title: Compound interest
subject: Personal finance
keywords: Rate, time, compounding frequency, and fees all matter.
summary: Interest calculated on principal plus accumulated interest.

title: Diversification
subject: Personal finance
keywords: It reduces some risk but cannot guarantee profit or eliminate market risk.
summary: Spreading investments across assets to reduce concentration risk.

title: Algorithm
subject: Computer science
keywords: Good algorithms are correct, clear, testable, and appropriately efficient.
summary: A finite ordered set of steps for solving a problem.

title: Variable and data type
subject: Programming
keywords: Types such as number, string, and Boolean determine valid operations.
summary: A named storage location whose value has a type.

title: Selection and iteration
subject: Programming
keywords: Conditions must be testable and loops need a correct stopping condition.
summary: Selection chooses among paths; iteration repeats instructions.

title: Function
subject: Programming
keywords: Functions improve decomposition, testing, reuse, and readability.
summary: A reusable block of code for a specific task, often with inputs and an output.

title: Testing and debugging
subject: Programming
keywords: Use normal, boundary, invalid, and edge cases.
summary: Testing checks behaviour; debugging finds and fixes the cause of failure.

title: Cybersecurity fundamentals
subject: Digital literacy
keywords: Use unique passwords, MFA, updates, backups, least privilege, and phishing awareness.
summary: Practices protecting systems, accounts, and data.

title: Engineering design process
subject: Technology
keywords: Use criteria, constraints, measurement, safety, sustainability, and user needs.
summary: Define, research, ideate, prototype, test, improve, and communicate.

title: Accessibility by design
subject: Technology
keywords: Consider keyboard navigation, captions, contrast, structure, labels, and alternatives.
summary: Designing so people with diverse abilities can use a product or environment.
